problems.statement: The gross daily-close quota (20, enforced with leaderboard shaming) rewards counting solve events rather than resolving problems, so agents game it with premature solves, ticket splitting and cherry-picking. This inflates ticket volume and reopens and is the main cause of the backlog doubling.

The backlog growth is mostly self-generated rework (reopens, split children, customer duplicates) and not real demand. First-contact issues rose only 4%, while the backlog of original first-contact tickets fell from 1,500 to 1,120 and rework grew from about 350 to about 2,780.

Cherry-picking of quick wins (saved filter, oldest-first dropping from 71% to 34%) leaves complex Tier-2 tickets aging badly, which is a distinct and costly harm to customers like Larkspur, whose bank-feed issue was repeatedly closed with the same help-article link.

The presented explanation, that the bar is too soft or agents are not working hard enough, is rejected. Closes per agent day rose from 11.7 to 19.0, and total closes exceed pre-quota levels, so effort and output measured by the metric went up while real resolution fell.

The shortfall is not an agent-capacity problem. Headcount and scheduled hours were flat (38 to 37 FTE, 6,020 to 5,960 hours), and the backlog was stable at the same capacity in Jan-Jun, so 12 more agents would mostly add more gamed closes.

The Payroll launch flooded the queue. This is rejected as a main cause: Payroll adds about 380 first-contact tickets per month (about 690 including rework), and 210 of 3,900 backlog tickets are Payroll-tagged, with a reopen rate in line with the queue average.

The reopen-rate rise is a measurement artefact caused by a changed auto-reopen-on-reply rule. This is rejected: the trigger and report definition are unchanged and courtesy-only replies are about 5% of reopens both before and after.

Attrition and pay competition (Corvane Fintech, deferred pay review, quota pressure) are a real emerging retention risk, with 58% considering leaving. Attrition has not yet reduced capacity because leavers were backfilled quickly, so it is not the backlog driver.

Rising engineering-side bugs (bank-feed sync after a banking-partner API change, 40 to 71 escalated bugs) may be keeping some complex tickets open and contributing to repeat contacts. The extent is unmeasured.

The exempt Billing-Compliance pod (no quota) stayed stable on volume, reopens, splits, pick order and aging while the same tooling, customers and managers applied elsewhere. This acts as a natural control that points to the quota rather than the platform or the environment.

causalClaims.from: Gross daily close quota with leaderboard consequences
causalClaims.to: Gaming behaviours (premature solves, ticket splitting, quick-win cherry-picking)
Rise in 14-day reopen rate (6% to 23%) and repeat-contact duplicates
Inflated ticket creation and backlog (split children 240 to 3,710)

causalClaims.from: Premature solves and aged complex tickets
causalClaims.to: Falling CSAT and customer churn risk

actions.action: Replace the gross close quota with a net-resolution measure. Count a ticket once per customer issue, give no credit for a reopened solve or a split child, and track 14-day reopen rate, age-weighted closes and CSAT as balancing measures.
actions.rationale: The metric is the mechanism of the harm, and Team C's partial fix already cut its reopen rate from 24% to 10%.

actions.action: Stop the leaderboard shaming and the non-negotiable-20 messaging, and tell leads that splits, reopen re-solves and premature solves will not be credited.
actions.rationale: Removing the pressure that makes gaming rational is quick and costs nothing.

actions.action: Merge split children back into parents, merge customer duplicates and re-triage the 1,180 reopened and 960 split tickets in the backlog, then restore oldest-first or age-weighted picking and retire or restrict the quick-wins filter.
actions.rationale: About 2,780 of the 3,900 backlog tickets are rework artefacts that can mostly be consolidated and closed properly.

actions.action: Run a focused sprint with Tier 2 and Integrations on the aged complex tickets (430 aged over 7 days). Link them to open engineering bugs and make the 'Waiting on engineering' status mandatory.
actions.rationale: Complex tickets and bank-feed issues drive customer damage (Larkspur, February renewal) and the engineering share is unmeasured.

actions.action: Contact Larkspur and similar at-risk accounts directly with a real fix owner.
actions.rationale: The renewal risk is concrete and time-bound.

actions.action: Escalate the tougher target with real consequences.
actions.rationale: More pressure on a gameable metric will increase splitting, premature solves and attrition (already 58% considering leaving).

actions.action: Approve the 12-agent request ($744,000 per year, permanent, with 16-18 weeks to productivity) now.
actions.rationale: Capacity is not the constraint, headcount cannot be withdrawn within the fiscal year, and new agents would face the same incentives.

actions.action: Revisit headcount only after the metric is fixed and the backlog is re-baselined, sized on first-contact demand (including Payroll) plus the engineering-driven complex work.
actions.rationale: True capacity need is unknown until rework is removed from the numbers.

actions.action: Bring forward the pay review or add a targeted retention measure for general-queue agents.
actions.rationale: The Corvane pay gap and the deferred review are a retention risk, but the evidence does not tie them to the backlog.

actions.action: Extend Team C's rule of not counting reopened closes to all teams as a stopgap while the new metric is built.
actions.rationale: It is partial (splits still count and complex aging still rose), but it is quick and shows a measurable effect.

nextEvidence: Link each of the 430 aged complex tickets to open engineering bugs, to size how much of the aging is waiting on engineering rather than on agent choice.
Re-baseline the backlog after merging splits and duplicates and re-triaging reopens, to measure true open first-contact work and the real weekly net inflow, including Payroll.
Team C and Billing pod follow-up after the metric change: net resolution, reopen rate, aged complex tickets, CSAT and agent time per complex ticket, to estimate the real capacity need.
output.summary: The backlog doubling is mostly caused by the quota itself. A gross-close target with leaderboard shaming rewards premature solves, ticket splitting and quick-win cherry-picking. Real first-contact demand rose only 4%, but reopens, split children and duplicates grew from about 350 to about 2,780 open tickets. Complex tickets aged, CSAT fell and 58% of agents are considering leaving. The unquota'd Billing pod was stable, and Team C improved when it stopped counting reopened closes. Effort, Payroll volume, capacity and a reopen-rule change are rejected. Do not toughen the target or fund 12 permanent agents. Fix the metric, consolidate rework, and clear complex tickets with engineering.
